title: Atlantic Bound
summary:
Atlantic Bound
A recent Wall Street Journal article indicated that US crude oil imports from Africa surpassed those of the Middle East in 2006, for the first time in over 20 years. The trend has been in place for the better part of the past 18 months. As recently as five years ago Middle East imports were substantially more than those from Africa.

children.section_path_text: Africa is in the Med Too!
children.summary: Interestingly, some of the largest contributors in Africa to this marked increase have not been West African players, but rather those with Mediterranean coastlines. Currently the largest exporter from these two regions is, not surprisingly, Saudi Arabia at a level of around 1.4 million barrels per day.

children.title: More Please
children.summary: The exports from West and North Africa are in addition to the Arabian Gulf crude supplies that are already established in the market. With this in mind, demand for vessels in the Arabian Gulf will remain firm as demand in the Atlantic Basin increases.
